correctness.rationale: The information matrix M=E[qq^T/(q^T S q)] has tr(SM)=1, proving lambda_min(M)<=1/tr S with equality iff M=I/tr S. Eigenvector law with mass lambda_i/tr S and sphere law w(q)=n q^T S q/tr S both realize equality. Metric-guided has M=S^{-1}/n; Haar has strictly larger min eigenvalue than metric guided but cannot be isotropic for nonscalar S (coordinate-swap identity). Planar circle integration gives m_i= lambda_i^{-(1+gamma)/2}/(a^{(1-gamma)/2}+b^{(1-gamma)/2}), isotropic uniquely gamma=-1 when a!=b. Independent numerical quadrature at S=diag(1,4),(1,9) confirmed the three strict levels; analytic trace proof covers all real SPD dimensions.
